# Create an askpass binary that answers passphrase prompts with the content
# of askpass.password. A file is used because the background agent does not
# see later env changes.
exec go build -o askpass-test askpass.go
env SSH_ASKPASS=./askpass-test
env SSH_ASKPASS_REQUIRE=force

exec ssh-tpm-agent -d --no-load --no-cache &agent&

# Create a key with one passphrase and change it to another
exec ssh-tpm-keygen -N oldpass
exec ssh-tpm-keygen -p -f .ssh/id_ecdsa.tpm -P oldpass -N newpass
stdout 'saved with the new passphrase'

exec ssh-tpm-add
stdout id_ecdsa.tpm

# The stored public key still matches the key file
exec ssh-tpm-keygen --print-pubkey .ssh/id_ecdsa.tpm
cp stdout printed.pub
cmp printed.pub .ssh/id_ecdsa.pub

# The old passphrase no longer works
cp oldpass askpass.password
! exec ssh-keygen -Y sign -n file -f .ssh/id_ecdsa.pub file_to_sign.txt
! exists file_to_sign.txt.sig

# The new passphrase does
cp newpass askpass.password
exec ssh-keygen -Y sign -n file -f .ssh/id_ecdsa.pub file_to_sign.txt
stdin file_to_sign.txt
exec ssh-keygen -Y check-novalidate -n file -f .ssh/id_ecdsa.pub -s file_to_sign.txt.sig
exists file_to_sign.txt.sig

-- file_to_sign.txt --
Hello World
-- oldpass --
oldpass
-- newpass --
newpass
-- go.mod --
module example.com/askpass

-- askpass.go --
package main

import (
  "fmt"
  "os"
  "strings"
)

func main() {
  if strings.Contains(os.Args[1], "passphrase") {
    b, err := os.ReadFile("askpass.password")
    if err != nil {
      os.Exit(1)
    }
    fmt.Println(strings.TrimSpace(string(b)))
  }
}
